measurement_interpretation.censoring: Action-cap survivors remain active RunState observations and are excluded from observed-terminal pressure/choice denominators.
measurement_interpretation.specialization_budget: Crew specializes through action 64, Numbers through action 112 after one real runner route, and pusher for 64 paid drops. They then return to the ordinary endgame driver so the global cap is a censoring guard rather than their planned ending.
measurement_interpretation.pusher: Unconditional natural availability plus reached-machine conditional distributions.
measurement_interpretation.specialists: Runs dynamically record conditioning when the policy selects a desired Crew contact who was not naturally present; such times are route-conditioned, not natural opportunity rates.
measurement_interpretation.heist: Completion distributions are conditional on audit_night and any recorded contact selection; they must not be read as natural opportunity frequency.
measurement_interpretation.legacy_control: Current quantitative control plus separate two-seed 0.5 structural compatibility evidence; no historical distribution inference.

source_register.contract: Exact data-defined economy register; production module paths remain authoritative for full-simulation paytables.

economy_checkpoint.scope: 0.6 sources and sinks visible at the content06_1 checkpoint

curves.numbers: Low ticket outlay repeats across a run; crew-fix cuts are intermittent income and must stay below a strong table session in aggregate.
curves.coin_pusher: Coin feed is the recurring sink; tray collection is the sole credit boundary. Prize riders and progressive cells are burst sources, not passive income.
curves.crew: Job stakes, components, and Mags cash costs are deliberate mid-run sinks; job rewards and successful cuts are bounded sources tied to completed play.
curves.heist: The Count risks three ordinary $8-30 blackjack sessions plus normal setup-route costs for a terminal $720-1,150 payout. The Whale requires $60 of qualifying losses, $120 of run-wide scored spending, a sourced False-Bottom Cup, and craps training; its 650-chip invitational pot moves through real game results and cashes once in a clamped $180-1,300 band.
curves.souvenirs: Scenario souvenirs enter free through one resolved event and sell for 4-14 cash; their value is memory plus a small existing-hook effect, never a primary income route.

new_sink_bands.heist_abort_formula: 15 + 10 per authored setup-state key, capped at bankroll - 1 so the run survives

heist_interactions.the_count: Identity sessions settle through ordinary blackjack, so their net wins/losses remain real run economy. Schedule and swap-cart setup use the normal travel/delivery framework. Outcome payout is flat by ladder rung: pinched 720, out hot 900, clean sweep 1,150.
heist_interactions.the_whale_game: The $120 name requirement reads existing run-wide scored spending rather than charging a second fee. The $60 vouch loss is real loss exposure. The rig prerequisite checks—but does not consume—the False-Bottom Cup and existing craps training. The seeded 650 chips become the authoritative pot, real mixed-game results grow or bust it, the finale clears the chips, then pays the clamped $180-1,300 pot once.
heist_interactions.abort: Before Play, abort charges 15 plus 10 for each stored setup-state key and caps payment at bankroll minus one. Abort does not end the run, but permanently closes both heist plans for that run.
heist_interactions.repeatability: Either completed plan ends Act 1 through the crew-heist victory route; abort is one-way. Neither payout is a repeatable farming source.

flagged_for_release06_1: Compare repeatable Numbers crew cuts against median Act 1 table profit after human playtest.
Measure pusher tray EV by variation with persisted loaded machines; do not infer EV from initial stock.
Check whether crew job rewards plus waived travel costs overfund the $32-44 cash bench band.
Compare The Count's $720/$900/$1,150 ladder against three identity-session outcomes and its two setup-route costs after human completion-time data.
Check The Whale's $180-1,300 pot payout against its real $60 loss requirement and overlapping $120 run-spending requirement; do not count the latter as a second direct fee.
Review whether the setup-key-count abort formula communicates a predictable cost as metadata keys accumulate, without changing its survivable bankroll cap in this pass.
Confirm free souvenir resale cannot be repeated through scenario revisit or save reload.

clock.ordering_contract: The handle resolves and posts at the Punchline at offset 16. Book closes are signed offsets from that post: negative closes before the post, zero at the post boundary, and positive remains open after the published handle. This explicit signed ordering is what makes physical past-posting possible.

slips.honest_ev_contract: Both products return less than stake in expectation. Straight gross return is 0.50 per dollar; the best-case distinct-digit box gross return is 0.42 per dollar. Repeated-digit boxes are worse.

leak.escalation_contract: Use the highest row whose successes threshold has been met; four or more stays on the final row. Effects begin on the next in-game day. Rumors carry the leaked number, declared pools grow but remain payout-capped, every Numbers venue gets twitchier, and the sweep reroute request is a seeded boundary roll.
